# Agent claim, implementation and handoff workflow

**AI disclosure:** This issue/document, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the repository owner's request.

This is the shared execution protocol for `ianrelecker/m365mcp`. It is adapted from [iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request#8](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/8) for agents working on this Microsoft 365 MCP server. It supplements repository instructions (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`); a ticket does not override those files or grant permission to hit live Microsoft Graph from tests, commit secrets, send mail without explicit user approval, add drive-item deletion tools, change Entra app permissions silently, or publish a release.

GitHub process ticket: [ianrelecker/m365mcp#21](https://github.com/ianrelecker/m365mcp/issues/21). Keep this file and that issue in sync when this process changes.

## Choose work

1. Read the repository README, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, this workflow, and the entire ticket. Implementation starts from `main`.
2. Choose **one leaf ticket** labeled `status:ready`. Epics and roadmaps coordinate work and are not implementation claims. Prefer P0, then P1 within your skills. The current ticket body and native blocked-by links are both authoritative; report inconsistencies before starting dependent work.
3. Read all comments, assignees, linked PRs and blockers. An unresolved prerequisite (including an open overlapping PR, a required live-tenant smoke, or an Entra permission change) must be satisfied before the dependent action. A completed research ticket only unblocks implementation when its approved design establishes feasibility; it does not mean the feature exists.
4. Tickets marked `status:backlog` can be promoted when their prerequisites and resources are satisfied. Record that decision. Do not skip or remove dependency links merely to make a ticket claimable.
5. Coordinate with already-open work before claiming overlapping files. Current examples to check: [#19](https://github.com/ianrelecker/m365mcp/pull/19) (PID-safe mode / Mail.Send default) and [#20](https://github.com/ianrelecker/m365mcp/pull/20) (dependency bumps).

## Claim without colliding

GitHub assignment alone is insufficient: several agents may share the same account. Use a unique session ID and preserve claims in comments.

Post a provisional comment with this structure:

```text
CLAIM
Agent/session: <unique session ID>
Ticket: <full issue URL>
Base commit: <SHA>
Branch/worktree: <branch and isolated local path>
Primary files/interfaces: <owned scope and expected overlaps>
Plan: <3-5 concrete steps tied to acceptance criteria>
Dependencies/resources checked: <links and evidence>
Live Graph/tenant: none | <account/tenant; scheduling need>
Lease expires: <UTC timestamp, at most 24 hours ahead>
```

Then re-read the issue comments and open PRs. The earliest still-valid claim by GitHub server comment ID owns the ticket; later competing claims must withdraw before editing. This is an optimistic coordination convention, **not an atomic lock**. If ownership is ambiguous, resolve it in the issue with the other claimant/coordinator before touching overlapping work. Never overwrite another agent's branch or worktree.

After confirming ownership, assign the authenticated account when permissions allow and move the ticket to `status:in-progress`. Record the session ID even when every agent uses `@me`. An example after ownership is confirmed:

```sh
gh issue edit <number> --repo ianrelecker/m365mcp --add-assignee @me \
  --remove-label status:ready --remove-label status:backlog \
  --add-label status:in-progress
```

One active implementation ticket per session. Renew your claim at each meaningful progress update and at least every four working hours, for no more than 24 hours ahead. Release explicitly when stopping. To take over an expired claim, first inspect the linked PR/latest comments and announce the takeover with a new session ID and branch. Preserve all prior work and state what will be reused; a stale timestamp never authorizes deleting it. A live PR or conflicting active work requires coordination.

## Isolate code and dependencies

- Use a dedicated worktree/branch, for example `agent/<ticket-number>-<short-topic>`, based on a freshly fetched `main`. Verify the worktree is clean before editing. Do not share a working directory between concurrent agents.
- List the actual files/interfaces you will change in your claim. Claims for different tickets do not grant ownership of the same shared core files. Coordinate these before overlapping edits:
  - `src/m365_mcp/server.py`
  - `src/m365_mcp/microsoft_graph.py`
  - `src/m365_mcp/microsoft_auth.py`
  - `src/m365_mcp/config.py`
  - `src/m365_mcp/models.py`
  - `src/m365_mcp/audit.py`
  - `manifest.json`
  - `M365_MCP_CAPABILITIES.md`
  - `tests/conftest.py`
  - package pins (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`) and release docs
- Follow the ticket's owning layer. Graph REST logic belongs in the graph/SharePoint/Excel clients, not in `server.py` tool wrappers. After adding, renaming, or removing a tool, run `uv run python scripts/sync_mcpb_tools.py`. Adding a required env var means matching `user_config` / `mcp_config.env` entries in `manifest.json`. Version bumps must update `manifest.json` and `pyproject.toml` together.
- Split an unexpectedly large ticket into linked implementation children before widening scope. Preserve the original acceptance criteria and dependency chain. Do not close a feature ticket when only its investigation is complete.

## Tenant, secrets, and live Graph are separate exclusive resources

An issue claim does not reserve a Microsoft 365 tenant, mailbox, or token file.

- Tests must stub HTTP. Do not call `graph.microsoft.com` from pytest. Follow the existing `httpx.AsyncClient` injection pattern.
- Do not commit `.env`, `.tokens/`, `.audit/`, client secrets, `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, refresh tokens, or mailbox contents. Never echo those values into issue comments, PR bodies, or logs.
- Do not run untrusted PR code against the owner's live tokens, helper port `8787`, or Entra app. A local token file is not a shared fixture.
- Prefer drafts over sending. `mail_send` / `mail_send_reply` require explicit user approval. SharePoint sharing mutations require `confirm=true`. Invitation email stays off by default.
- There must be **no** tool that deletes a SharePoint/OneDrive drive item. `Files.ReadWrite.All` permits it at Graph level; this repo still forbids it. Do not add `Sites.ReadWrite.All`.
- Do not change the hardcoded Graph scope list in `config.py` without updating `tests/conftest.py` and documenting the Entra admin-consent impact in the PR.
- Live-tenant smoke (OAuth helper, Claude Desktop, real mailboxes) is optional evidence and must be scheduled with the owner. It is not a substitute for offline tests.

## Implement and prove

1. Establish the smallest relevant baseline and reproduce a claimed bug before editing when feasible. Record source/tool identity. Do not use production mailboxes as scratch space.
2. Add a meaningful regression and implement the bounded fix. For new tools, prove the Graph path, the MCP wrapper, audit classification/redaction, and (if user-facing) `M365_MCP_CAPABILITIES.md` plus `manifest.json` stay in sync.
3. Offline baseline:

   ```sh
   uv sync --extra dev
   uv run pytest
   ```

   After tool or manifest changes:

   ```sh
   uv run python scripts/sync_mcpb_tools.py
   uv run pytest tests/test_manifest.py tests/test_mcp_server.py
   ```

4. Run ticket-specific tests, not just the suite total. Preserve known failures and skipped live-Graph cases. Do not count a mocked HTTP 200 as proof of a working Entra consent, Desktop install, or shared-mailbox permission.
5. Provide commands, expected/actual output, dependency versions, and (when relevant) Graph request path plus status. Keep tokens, mailbox addresses that are not already public, message bodies, subjects, and attachment bytes out of public artifacts.

## PR, review and completion

- Open a scoped PR early as draft and link the ticket and dependency PRs. Include the problem, resulting behavior, meaningful before/after evidence, limitations and each acceptance criterion's status.
- The owner requested this disclosure for every AI-authored PR: **"This pull request, including its title and every word of this description, was generated by AI."** Preserve original authorship/credits for imported changes.
- Mark `status:review` when the concrete result and required evidence are ready. Passing CI (`uv run pytest` on Python 3.10–3.13) alone does not satisfy missing live-tenant, Desktop-install, or release criteria.
- Prefer a separate agent/human review for auth, token storage, audit redaction, Graph scopes, sharing, and send-mail changes when available; record whether review was independent. Never claim a self-check was independent review.
- Use `Fixes <full issue URL>` only for a fully completed leaf task. Use `Refs` for partial work, research parents, or integration not yet validated. Default-branch auto-close must not hide unmet criteria.
- Close a task as completed only after its code/docs are merged into `main` and all criteria have evidence. For research, attach the accepted decision and required implementation children; mark unsupported features honestly. A blocked or impossible implementation stays blocked or is explicitly closed as not planned with rationale, never as delivered support.
- Final handoff: commits/PRs, each criterion and evidence, tests not run and why, known risks, next exact command/step, any live-tenant sessions still open, and release/renewal of the claim. Update native dependencies and readiness on directly unblocked children. Epics close only when their promised outcomes and required children are complete.

## Status and priority meanings

- `status:ready`: scoped, prerequisites satisfied, claimable within listed permissions/resources.
- `status:backlog`: planned but outside the first wave or awaiting prioritization/resource arrangement.
- `status:blocked`: a named dependency, tenant/authorization or unresolved design prevents required work.
- `status:in-progress`: one identified agent owns active implementation.
- `status:review`: concrete result awaits review, checks or integration. Close only after acceptance.
- `priority:P0`: release-blocking correctness/safety or essential evidence infrastructure (auth, token encryption, audit redaction, accidental send/delete).
- `priority:P1`: important compatibility, reliability or delivery work.
- `priority:P2`: extended coverage, optimization or optional live-tenant expansion.

Sizes S/M/L describe relative review scope, not promised hours. A status change must include the concrete reason when it alters another agent's ability to start.

Source protocol: [iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request#8](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/8).
